# Onboarding Guide

Welcome to the **eap-ref-architecture** repository — Gainwell Technologies' Enterprise Architecture Reference Repository.
page_texts.2:
[onboarding/README.md#quick-start]

## Quick Start

This repository includes automated setup scripts to configure your development environment with all required tools and extensions for contributing to enterprise architecture documentation.
page_texts.4:
[onboarding/README.md#macos--linux]

#### macOS / Linux

1. Open a terminal in the repository root
2. Run the setup script:

```bash
./onboarding/setup-mac.sh
```
page_texts.5:
[onboarding/README.md#windows]

#### Windows

1. Open a terminal on Windows (PowerShell is built in on modern Windows)
2. Navigate to the repository root
3. Run one setup command:

```powershell
.\onboarding\setup-windows.ps1
```

[onboarding/README.md#mcp-server-setup]

## MCP Server Setup

MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers give AI assistants (Copilot and Claude Code) direct access to external platforms from chat. Both servers work with Copilot Agent mode and Claude Code — no separate configuration needed per assistant.

The workspace includes a `.vscode/mcp.json` that configures both servers. No global npm packages are installed.
page_texts.16:
[onboarding/README.md#mcp-servers]

#### MCP Servers

| Server | Package | Type | Auth | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **GitHub** | Remote (GitHub-hosted) | HTTP | Copilot OAuth (automatic) | Official GitHub MCP Server. Provides full GitHub API access: create/review PRs, manage branches, search code, create/update issues, list commits, merge PRs, fork repos, and manage releases. No local install — hosted at `api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/` |
| **Azure DevOps** | `@azure-devops/mcp` | stdio (npx) | Browser login on first use | Official Microsoft ADO MCP Server. Provides work item CRUD, user story creation, sprint/iteration queries, board management, repo browsing, and wiki access. Auto-downloaded by `npx` on first use — no global install |
page_texts.17:
[onboarding/README.md#ado-domain-filtering]

#### ADO Domain Filtering

The ADO server is configured with domains `core`, `work`, and `work-items` to keep the tool count manageable and avoid confusing the AI model.

| Domain | What it provides |
|---|---|
| `core` | Project listing, team info, organization-level queries |
| `work` | Iterations, sprints, boards, backlogs, team capacity |
| `work-items` | Create, read, update, and query work items (user stories, bugs, tasks, features) |

Additional domains can be enabled by editing `.vscode/mcp.json`:

| Domain | What it adds |
|---|---|
| `search` | Full-text search across code, work items, and wiki |
| `test-plans` | Test plans, test suites, and test cases |
| `repositories` | Git repos, branches, commits, pull requests within ADO |
| `wiki` | Create, read, and update wiki pages |
| `pipelines` | Build and release pipeline management |
| `advanced-security` | Security alerts and dependency scanning |
page_texts.18:
[onboarding/README.md#using-mcp-servers]

#### Using MCP Servers

1. Open Copilot Chat or Claude Code in VS Code
2. Switch to **Agent mode**
3. The servers start automatically — ADO will prompt for your org name on first use
4. Try prompts like:
    - "List my open PRs on GitHub"
    - "Create a user story in ADO project 'Contoso'"
    - "Show work items in the current sprint for 'Contoso'"
    - "List ADO repos for 'Contoso'"
page_texts.19:
[onboarding/README.md#ai-assistant-setup-during-onboarding]

## AI Assistant Setup During Onboarding

Both setup scripts install GitHub Copilot by default.

Claude Code setup is **optional** — the scripts will ask:
> "Would you like to set up Claude Code? (y/N)"

If you choose yes, Claude Code is configured with AWS Bedrock:

1. Installs the Claude Code VS Code extension
2. Validates the AWS profile (`dev`) exists in your AWS CLI config
3. Validates STS access (`aws sts get-caller-identity`)
4. Validates Bedrock access in `us-east-1`
5. Persists environment variables (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `AWS_PROFILE`, `AWS_REGION`) to your shell profile
6. Updates `~/.claude/settings.json` with Bedrock config and default permissions using `AWS_PROFILE` delegation (no raw credentials stored)
7. Model selection is handled by the Claude Code extension — use `/model` within Claude Code to choose your preferred model

Copilot and Claude Code run side by side with no conflicts. If any Bedrock prerequisite fails, the script continues — Copilot remains fully functional.

## Package Manager Preference

- **macOS**: Homebrew is the preferred package manager and is installed/updated by the script.
- **Windows**: Chocolatey is the preferred package manager and is installed/used by the script.

[onboarding/README.md#vs-code-configuration-standards]

## VS Code Configuration Standards

This repository includes a `.vscode/settings.json` file that maintains consistent configuration standards across all team members. When you open this repository in VS Code, these settings are automatically applied to ensure:
page_texts.22:
[onboarding/README.md#consistency-across-the-team]

### Consistency Across the Team

- **Indentation**: Standardized to 2 spaces for most file types (4 for Python)
- **Line Endings**: Normalized to LF (Unix-style) for cross-platform compatibility
- **Encoding**: UTF-8 for all files
- **Trailing Whitespace**: Automatically trimmed on save
page_texts.23:
[onboarding/README.md#markdown-standards]

### Markdown Standards

- **Line Length**: Wrapped at 100 characters for readability
- **Linting**: MarkdownLint rules enforce consistent formatting
- **Preview**: GitHub-flavored markdown rendering
- **Auto-formatting**: Prettier formats markdown on save
page_texts.24:
[onboarding/README.md#code-quality]

### Code Quality

- **Auto-save**: Configured with appropriate delay
- **Format on Save**: Ensures code is always properly formatted
- **Spell Checking**: Enabled for documentation files
- **Git Integration**: Enhanced with GitLens
page_texts.25:
[onboarding/README.md#why-this-matters]

### Why This Matters

The shared `.vscode/settings.json` file ensures that:

1. **All team members see the same formatting** - No more "fixing" formatting that another editor changed
2. **Pull requests stay clean** - Only meaningful changes appear in diffs, not formatting differences
3. **Documentation is consistent** - Same markdown style, line lengths, and structure
4. **Onboarding is faster** - New team members automatically get the right configuration
5. **Best practices are enforced** - Spell checking, linting, and formatting happen automatically

These workspace settings override individual user settings only for this repository, so your personal VS Code preferences remain unchanged in other projects.

### eap-ref-architecture Context

This repository is a **documentation repository** focused on:

- Architecture standards, patterns, and principles
- Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)
- Strategic guidance and best practices
- Governance processes and frameworks
- Training and enablement materials

**What's NOT in this repository:**

- Application source code (see product-specific repositories)
- Infrastructure-as-Code deployments (see product-specific IaC repositories)
- Operational runbooks (see ITSM repositories)
page_texts.29:
[onboarding/README.md#document-conversion-tools]

### Document Conversion Tools

The `.utils/` folder contains Python-based document conversion tools for working with architecture documentation in multiple formats (Markdown, PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel). These tools help:

- Convert existing Word/PDF documents to Markdown for version control
- Generate professional PDFs from Markdown documentation
- Convert presentation slides to Markdown for searchability
- Extract Excel data into Markdown tables

See `.utils/README.md` for complete documentation on available tools and usage.
